findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the tail-handler's 'post-push GET → store true remote as baseline' with the '_advance_baselines is sole baseline writer' invariant: specify that the GET result feeds through set_baseline/_advance_baselines (or explicitly designate a second, ordered writer).
evidence: Plan: 'do ONE post-push GET for that field and store the true remote as baseline. `_advance_baselines` (`reconcile_helpers.py:602`) stays sole baseline writer'
reconcile_helpers.py:632 set_baseline is called only inside _advance_baselines; no post-push-GET baseline path exists in the code today (search for 'post-push' returned no matches)
findings.finding: The 'non-idempotent tail' handler prescribes 'ONE post-push GET for that field and store the true remote as baseline,' but the same section asserts '_advance_baselines (reconcile_helpers.py:602) stays sole baseline writer.' A per-field post-push GET that writes a baseline is a second baseline-write path, contradicting the sole-writer invariant; the plan does not reconcile the two (e.g. by routing the GET result through _advance_baselines / set_baseline rather than a new writer).
findings.location: Context / Problem — 'non-idempotent tail is bounded' paragraph
scenarios: A description body falls in the non-idempotent tail and the tail-handler writes a baseline outside _advance_baselines
findings.suggested_fix: State that the tail's post-push GET result is handed to _advance_baselines' synced_fields overlay (merge_baseline) for that field, keeping _advance_baselines the sole writer.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify where the 'field was re-emitted on the immediately-preceding pass' signal is stored and how 'second consecutive pass with rich_sha unchanged' is evaluated (including the first-pass / absent-rich_sha case), so tail detection is deterministic and cannot loop or fire every pass.
evidence: Plan: 'if a binding re-emits the same field on a second consecutive pass with `rich_sha` unchanged, it is in the tail'
Plan stores only 'a change-gated rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16] inline in the binding'; no field records 'emitted-last-pass'
Design decision 4: 'the compare never writes back' — so the compare cannot itself record the prior-pass emit signal
findings.finding: The tail-detection predicate — 're-emits the same field on a second consecutive pass with rich_sha unchanged' — is an across-pass check-then-act that needs the previous pass's 're-emitted this field' signal to be persisted and read on the next pass, but the plan only specifies storing rich_sha inline; it never says where the 'was re-emitted on the immediately-preceding pass' state lives or how consecutiveness is determined.
findings.location: Context / Problem — 'if a binding re-emits the same field on a second consecutive pass with rich_sha unchanged'
scenarios: Two non-consecutive re-emits of the same body (e.g. an intervening no-op pass) — is that 'second consecutive'?
First-ever pass where rich_sha is absent: the predicate 'rich_sha unchanged' has no prior value to compare

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the hallucinated `_compute_field_changes` reference with the real diff entry point (`diff_canonical_fields`, outbound_field_diff.py:278, reached via `map_remote_to_local`) so the 'reused unchanged' baseline-diff path is grounded in a symbol that exists.
evidence: search_files for `_compute_field_changes` and `compute_field_changes` both returned (no matches)
outbound_field_diff.py:278 defines/calls `diff_canonical_fields` as the actual field-diff driver; `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` is at outbound_field_diff.py:47 and outbound_fields.py:275
The other named diff/gate helpers (`_suppressed_by_inbound`, `_local_matches_baseline`, `_remote_matches_baseline`) all resolve, so this is an isolated hallucinated symbol, not a mislabeled module
findings.finding: The 'Reused unchanged' section cites `_compute_field_changes` as the mechanism by which `description` (in `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS`) participates in the ADR-0026/d6bd baseline diff, but no symbol named `_compute_field_changes` (or `compute_field_changes`) exists anywhere in the repository. The actual per-field diff entry point in outbound_field_diff.py is `diff_canonical_fields` (line 278), invoked from `map_remote_to_local`/the InboundMapper path (lines 260-292).
findings.location: Context / Problem — 'Reused unchanged' paragraph (`description` in `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` `:47`, via `_compute_field_changes`)
scenarios: An implementer trying to locate the reused diff path to confirm it is untouched will search for `_compute_field_changes` and find nothing, undermining the 'reused unchanged' guarantee

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the failure behavior of the tail-recovery post-push GET (leave baseline unadvanced and retry next pass vs. surface the error), so a transient GET failure cannot break convergence or persist a stale baseline.
evidence: The plan adds a post-push GET as a new failure point on the write/reconcile path but gives no error handling for it.
Sole-writer _advance_baselines is specified, but the failure mode of the extra GET is not.
findings.finding: The non-idempotent-tail recovery does a network GET ('do ONE post-push GET for that field and store the true remote as baseline') but the plan does not specify what happens if that GET fails (network error / timeout) — whether the baseline is left unadvanced and retried next pass, or written stale.
findings.location: Context / Problem — 'do ONE post-push GET for that field and store the true remote as baseline'
scenarios: The post-push GET times out or errors; baseline is left in an undefined state, potentially causing a re-emit loop or a stale baseline.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the pandoc/pypandoc precondition for the DC cutover and add a DC-side AC/test for the pandoc-absent case (analogous to the marklas-absent AC), pinning that render_markdown_to_wiki degrades to plain wire without raising.
evidence: render_markdown_to_wiki docstring: 'Returns the input unchanged when pandoc is unavailable'
_pandoc_path (wiki_render.py:134) returns None on ImportError of pypandoc or OSError from get_pandoc_path; _convert (wiki_render.py:325) shells out to the pandoc binary
DC AC asserts 'issue.update(fields=…) gets rendered wiki, not raw Markdown' but pandoc-absent makes render_markdown_to_wiki return raw Markdown
Cloud path has an explicit degradation AC ('With the marklas extra absent … emits the plain-text ADF wire') with no DC/pandoc counterpart
Evidence class: Partially-verified — the pandoc integration exists in-repo with fallback, but the plan does not state the precondition or the DC-side absent behavior
findings.finding: The DC cutover depends on pandoc (via render_markdown_to_wiki → pypandoc.get_pandoc_path / subprocess), but the plan states no pandoc environment precondition and no pandoc-absent degradation behavior, while the Cloud path has an explicit marklas-absent AC.
findings.location: Scope / Acceptance Criteria (DC bullets: test_dc_cutover_converges); final marklas-absent AC
scenarios: A DC client runs the cutover on a host/wheel where pandoc (pypandoc) is not installed
CI/canary runs the DC converge test in an environment lacking the pandoc binary
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion mirroring the marklas one: 'With pandoc/pypandoc absent, the DC cutover path ships the plain (identity) wire and raises nothing; a test simulates the missing pandoc with the flag ON.' Also note pandoc as an environment precondition (or confirm it is wheel-bundled) in Scope.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether rich_sha's 16-hex-char digest should route through an existing hashing helper or is intentionally a standalone hashlib.sha256 over the rendered wire string (state which, and why the existing content_hash seam does/doesn't fit).
evidence: Plan: 'Store a change-gated rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16] (8 bytes) inline in the binding'
conflict_resolver.py:214 _hash_value routes through content_hash (mutation.py) as 'the canonical seam'; manifest_renderer.py:161 and impossible_links.py:197/241 each call hashlib.sha256 directly
The existing content_hash seam is JSON-value/ascii-only oriented, so it may not fit a raw wire-string+truncation use — this is a confirm-reuse note, not an asserted rebuild
findings.finding: The rich_sha computation (sha256(rendered_wire)[:16]) may inline a raw hashlib call when a canonical hashing seam already exists in the reconciler.
findings.location: Design decisions #4 (rich_sha) / Scope (IN) binding_store.py inline rich_sha
scenarios: Implementation adds a fourth independent hashlib.sha256 call-site with its own truncation convention rather than a shared helper

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the line citations for `_remote_matches_baseline` (actual outbound_field_diff.py:483) and `_emit_outbound_field_alerts` (actual run_differs.py:81) so the edit targets point at the real definitions.
evidence: search_files: outbound_field_diff.py:483 `def _remote_matches_baseline(` (plan says :399)
search_files: run_differs.py:81 `def _emit_outbound_field_alerts(` (plan says :97; :483 is only a call site)
findings.finding: Two load-bearing line-number citations point at the wrong lines: `_remote_matches_baseline` is cited at `:399` but is defined at outbound_field_diff.py:483, and `run_differs._emit_outbound_field_alerts` is cited at `:97` but is defined at run_differs.py:81. The symbols exist (so not hallucinated), but the offsets are large enough to send an implementer to unrelated code.
scenarios: Implementer jumps to outbound_field_diff.py:399 / run_differs.py:97 and finds unrelated code, slowing the edit or editing the wrong hunk

findings.finding: The inline change-gated rich_sha is a new stored artifact whose only acceptance criterion is a storage-cost profile; no suppression/convergence AC reads it, so its current-done-definition purpose is unstated (YAGNI risk).
findings.location: Design decisions #4 ('Store a change-gated rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16] inline in the binding') and the AC 'The rich layer stores an inline change-gated 8-byte rich_sha ... verified by the git-delta harness at <=0.07 KB/version'

findings.finding: The plan identifies backend.py:_map_local_to_dc_fields as the DC CREATE path that fits description without rendering (needs to_wire before fit), but a SECOND DC create-side path with the identical defect is not enumerated: adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py builds `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC = WikiTextCodec()` (:40) and applies only `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound(description)` (:111) inside `_translate_create_fields` (:93), which is invoked by `create_issue` (:174). Post-cutover this path ships RAW Markdown on DC create, defeating the 'issue.update/CREATE gets rendered wiki' guarantee for issues created through the REST client.
findings.location: The live cutover → DC (CREATE) section; Scope (IN)
findings.suggested_fix: Add `_issues.py` to Scope (IN) alongside backend.py's CREATE path and require the same render-before-fit change (gated), plus a create-through-_issues convergence assertion.

findings.finding: The DC CREATE-path patch-site inventory for the WikiTextCodec render-before-fit change is incomplete: the plan names only _map_local_to_dc_fields (backend.py:57), but a second, independent create-time description fit-only site — _translate_create_fields (_issues.py:93) using _DESCRIPTION_CODEC = WikiTextCodec() (_issues.py:40), fitting via _DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound(description) at _issues.py:111 — is the site actually invoked by the transport create_issue (_issues.py:174 -> client.create_issue(**fields)) and is omitted from both the CREATE discussion and Scope (IN). It applies fit_outbound without to_wire/render exactly as the plan's own rationale describes for the CREATE site it does patch.
findings.location: The live cutover → DC bullet: 'CREATE is separate: _map_local_to_dc_fields (adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:57) builds its OWN WikiTextCodec() and applies only codec.fit_outbound(...), never to_wire, so it must also render before the fit' and Scope (IN): 'the backend.py (:70) CREATE path'
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the CREATE bullet and Scope (IN) to cover _issues.py: apply the same render-before-fit (render Markdown to wiki, then _DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound) at _issues.py:111, gated by the same flag, and add the _issues.py module to the scoped files with a create-convergence test.

findings.finding: The rollback/cutover flag — a new config/flag that AC8 requires to default OFF and that both the Cloud and DC cutover Scope lines call 'gated' — has no named edit target in the Scope edit-set. It is a CREATION (new behavioral surface) that gates the codec-selection/send path, yet no config module or symbol is enumerated to define/read it.
findings.location: Scope section (Cloud/DC '(gated)' lines) + Rollback paragraph + AC8 (test_cutover_defaults_off / test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain)
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Scope bullet naming where the flag is defined (e.g., a REBAR_RECONCILER_RICH_TEXT_CUTOVER_<CLIENT> constant in src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py) and the exact read site(s) that select the Markdown-aware vs plain/identity path per client, so AC8's tests have a named target.

findings.finding: Once-only convergence is staked entirely on the codec law plus marklas's 99.65% round-trip idempotence with 'no post-push GET', but the ~0.35% non-idempotent tail is unhandled: for a body where decode(to_wire(local)) != decode(wire Jira echoes back), the normalized local never matches decode(baseline_wire), so local!=baseline holds every pass and the description re-emits forever with no bounded-re-emit or churn-detection guard.
findings.location: Context/Problem ('hence no post-push GET') and Design decisions #1; Acceptance Criteria (test_lossy_body_converges_across_passes / test_recanonicalization_converges)
findings.suggested_fix: Add a change-gated re-emit guard keyed on the stored rich_sha: once a description has been pushed and its wire echo has been baselined, suppress a further identical push unless local (not its normalization) actually changed, so a non-idempotent body re-emits at most once instead of every pass; cover it with a test using a deliberately non-idempotent codec stub.
